claim: Across 166 purchase months (2003-01 to 2016-11), a 10-year TIPS held to maturity inside an IRA returned exactly its real yield, which was negative only when the yield itself was negative (18 months). The same bond in a taxable account, with 24% federal tax each year on both the coupon and the inflation adjustment, ended with a negative real after-tax return in 64 of 166 months (38.6%). The yearly tax drag ran from 0.39 to 1.13 percentage points (median 0.8); $10,000 grew to a median $11,480 in real terms inside the IRA versus $10,658 in the taxable account. Worst taxable case: bought 2012-11, -1.18% a year after tax and inflation (IRA: -0.77%). In 2022 a $10,000 holding with the minimum coupon owed $188.89 of federal tax on a 7.75% inflation adjustment while paying $12.5 in cash; the tax exceeded the cash coupon in 8 of 22 years. History, not a forecast.

numbers.definition: Number of purchase months 2003-01..2016-11 simulated (one skipped). Model: for each purchase month m from 2003-01 to 2016-11, an idealized 10-year TIPS bought at par whose real value grows at the real yield y = FII10 value for month m (percent/100) each year, compounded annually, and whose principal is indexed by the reference CPI ref(x) = CPIAUCNS value three months before month x. Year k (k = 0..9) inflation factor f_k = ref(m+12(k+1)) / ref(m+12k); nominal growth factor g_k = (1+y) * f_k. Taxable account: W_{k+1} = W_k * (1 + 0.76*(g_k - 1)) (24% tax on the whole year's nominal increase, coupon plus inflation accrual, paid from the holding; negative increases reduce tax symmetrically). IRA (no yearly tax, Roth-equivalent): W_{k+1} = W_k * g_k. Real ending value = W_10 / product(f_k); annualized real return = (real ending value)^(1/10) - 1. Purchase months whose annual checkpoints need the unpublished October 2025 CPI are skipped (only 2016-01).

Federal tax for 2022 on $10,000 of inflation-adjusted principal with coupon c = max(FII10 for 2022-01, 0.125)/100 (0.125% is the minimum TIPS coupon): 0.24 * 10000 * (c + inflation accrual 2022). Coupon on the adjusted principal ignored. Rounded to cents.

Count of calendar years Y in 2003-2024 for which 0.24*10000*(c_Y + a_Y) > 10000*c_Y, where c_Y = max(FII10 for Y-01, 0.125)/100 and a_Y = CPIAUCNS(Y-10)/CPIAUCNS((Y-1)-10) - 1 (October to October). 2025 is excluded because October 2025 CPI was never published.
Number of calendar years checked (2003-2024).

assumptions: Federal marginal rate 24% in every year, applied to the full nominal increase (coupon plus inflation accrual) in the year it accrues; tax paid out of the holding. No state tax (TIPS interest is exempt from state income tax).

Idealized bond bought at par at the monthly-average 10-year real yield (FII10); real return compounding annually; no premium or discount, no bid-ask cost; negative real yields treated as negative real growth.
Inflation indexation uses CPI-U NSA with a three-month lag (monthly, not daily interpolation). The unpublished October 2025 CPI is not filled in; affected cases are skipped.
Negative annual accruals (deflation) reduce taxable income one-for-one (simplification of the OID/deflation rules).
IRA case is untaxed growth (Roth-equivalent); a traditional IRA gives the same result if the tax rate at withdrawal equals the rate at contribution.
Held to maturity, ten annual steps.

provisions.cite: IRS Publication 550, Inflation-Indexed Debt Instruments (inflation adjustments to TIPS principal are taxable each year as OID; 26 CFR 1.1275-7)
provisions.quote: If you hold an inflation-indexed debt instrument (other than a series I U.S. savings bond), you must report as OID any increase in the inflation-adjusted principal amount of the instrument that occurs while you held the instrument during the year.
These securities pay interest twice a year at a fixed rate, based on a principal amount adjusted to take into account inflation and deflation.
